1keig3f:424: AgentCore's quality optimization flywheel represents a fundamental paradigm shift from intuition-driven to data-driven development. Traditional AI agent optimization relies heavily on developer personal experience—reading traces, forming hypotheses, rewriting prompts, testing on a few cases, and then deploying. This manual loop is not only inefficient but also prone to introducing new problems; especially without automated feedback mechanisms, every fix may create new edge cases for another class of users. AgentCore's new capabilities build a complete automated optimization loop through three core components: Recommendations learns from production traces and evaluation outputs to automatically generate optimization suggestions for system prompts or tool descriptions targeting specific evaluators; Batch Evaluation validates recommendation quality offline using predefined test datasets; A/B Testing runs statistically significant controlled experiments on production traffic through the AgentCore Gateway. This "observe-evaluate-improve" three-stage loop shortens the optimization cycle from weeks to days while ensuring every decision is data-backed rather than subjective.

2p6489:238: From an architectural perspective, AgentCore decouples configuration from code—configurations are stored as immutable versioned bundles containing runtime parameters such as model ID, system prompt, and tool descriptions, and agents dynamically read the active configuration via the SDK. This means switching prompts or models is simply a configuration change rather than a code change, greatly reducing the complexity of experimentation and rollback. Combined with an OpenTelemetry-compatible trace collection mechanism, every model invocation, tool call, and reasoning step is fully recorded, providing rich raw data for Recommendations analysis and optimization.
4prf97:221: : Before adopting AgentCore, teams should first define their reward signal—the core metric for measuring agent quality. AgentCore supports built-in evaluators (goal success rate, tool selection accuracy, usefulness, safety) and custom LLM-as-judge scoring systems. It is recommended to define evaluation dimensions and establish ground-truth comparison baselines from the very beginning, as this will directly affect the optimization direction of subsequent Recommendations. Without clear evaluation criteria, data-driven optimization is impossible.

This evolution path reflects the inevitable trend of AI agent operations shifting from manual work to automation at scale.

k5dsic:168: : The key value of Batch Evaluation lies in regression testing—ensuring that every configuration change does not break existing known-good cases. It is recommended to integrate Batch Evaluation into the CI/CD pipeline so that any configuration bundle must pass the quality threshold of a preset test set before reaching production. This "gate" mechanism effectively prevents the accumulation of negative optimizations, allowing teams to maintain iteration speed without sacrificing quality stability.

ts7y41:199: : When running A/B tests online, you need to configure the traffic split ratio properly to balance statistical significance and business risk. The practices of NTT DATA and Nomura Research Institute show that deriving improvement suggestions from production trace data and then validating their actual impact with A/B testing enables efficient improvement at scale while ensuring accuracy and validity. It is recommended to start with a small traffic ratio (e.g., 5-10%) in the early phase, and make statistically significant judgments only after enough data has been accumulated.
